answer: A marble registry of one-identity-per-device stops sybils cheaply: each agent must present a manufacturer-signed attestation key burned into silicon, and the chain keeps a nullifier set so a second registration with the same root fails. Honest agents register once; a farmer buying a thousand clones must source a thousand physical units and still cannot reuse a key. Reputation accrues only to registered roots, so an ivory certificate of standing cannot be minted on demand, and the karst of duplicate registrations collapses under its own weight.
